title: Live API response state
description: Schema for analysis/handoff/live_api_response.json — the per-row outcome record produced by scripts/backlog_live_apply.py (Phase 3, Section C, closes TODO-S9-LIVE-API). One file per (workspace, platform) pair. Idempotency state: re-running backlog_live_apply against an unchanged export reads this file, skips already-created rows by idempotency_key, and only POSTs the missing ones. Strictly read-only with respect to canonical state. F5-validated so a malformed response file (wrong schema, missing provenance, broken idempotency key) fails the write rather than landing as a corrupt state file. Tokens are NEVER persisted here — only platform_base_url + the operator's run_id + per-row idempotency keys + created issue references.

schema_version.description: Live-API response shape version. Bumped on breaking shape changes; consumers can pin to a known major version. Format: bare semver (no canon-policy hash; the response is downstream of canonical state, not part of it).

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when this run completed (success or partial failure). Same shape as marker.timestamp.

platform.description: Platform discriminator. Tied to which export file was consumed (backlog_export_jira.json, backlog_export_linear.csv, backlog_export_github.csv).

platform_base_url.description: Base URL of the live API instance (e.g., https://acme.atlassian.net for Jira; https://api.linear.app for Linear; https://api.github.com for GitHub). Recorded so an operator can audit which instance the export landed in. Tokens are NEVER recorded here — only the public base URL.

operator_run_id.description: Operator-supplied run identifier (CLI flag --run-id=<id>, or auto-generated from timestamp + workspace name). Lets two operators distinguish their concurrent runs against the same instance. Lowercase alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore.

source_export_path.description: Workspace-relative path to the export file consumed (e.g., 'analysis/handoff/backlog_export_jira.json'). Pin to the live canonical state at the time of run for drift detection.

source_export_canon_hash.description: Optional. canon_policy_version hash_prefix at the time of the run. Captures which canonical policy state the export was generated from. Helpful for cross-referencing with audit_expectations on regression tests.

results.description: One element per export row processed in this run. Empty array allowed when the export contained zero rows (early Phase-3 runs).

total.description: Total rows in the export consumed by this run.

created.description: Rows that resulted in a NEW platform-side resource (HTTP 2xx).

skipped.description: Rows skipped because the idempotency_key was already present in a prior live_api_response.json (re-run safety).

failed.description: Rows that failed after retry budget exhausted. Each failure carries last_error in its result_row.

summary.description: Aggregate counts. Operator can read this without scanning the full results array. total = created + skipped + failed by invariant.

story_id.description: A70.StoryID this row maps to. Provenance carry-through from the export.

idempotency_key.description: Per-row idempotency key. Format: bsa-{StoryID}-{canon_hash_prefix}. Re-runs of backlog_live_apply against the same StoryID + same canonical policy state will see the key in a prior live_api_response.json and skip. Changing the canonical state (canon hash moves) produces a new key, which the platform may treat as a new issue (operator must reconcile via platform-side dedup if needed).

status.description: Outcome. created = HTTP 2xx + platform_id captured. skipped = prior run's idempotency_key was found; no HTTP call this run. failed = retry budget exhausted; last_error populated.

platform_id.description: Platform-side identifier of the created resource (Jira issue key 'BSA-123'; Linear issue identifier 'OPS-456'; GitHub issue number '789' as string). Empty when status=failed. Token-shaped strings (JWT, GitHub PAT, Atlassian API token, Bearer/Basic credentials) are explicitly REJECTED here — defense-in-depth against accidental token persistence (Codex v1.1.6 round-1 should-fix #2).

platform_url.description: Optional. Browseable URL the operator can open in a browser to inspect the created resource. When platform_base_url + platform_id are both present, the script computes this from a per-platform pattern. Token-shaped strings explicitly rejected (a query-string token would be a leak).

attempts.description: Number of HTTP attempts made for this row. 0 = skipped (idempotency hit). 1 = first attempt succeeded. >1 = retry-with-backoff occurred. Capped at 10 to bound runtime against pathological 5xx loops.

last_error.description: When status=failed, the last error message captured. Tokens are SCRUBBED before recording (Authorization header values replaced with <REDACTED>) AND the schema explicitly rejects token-shaped strings here — defense-in-depth against the scrub regex missing a novel token shape (Codex v1.1.6 round-1 should-fix #2).
